{{ds:component/alert|variant=warning|title=Shared connectors|body_html=

A connector referenced by multiple pipelines is rotated once, for all of them. Check a connector's pipeline_count field before rotating during a busy window.

{ "item": { "id": "5ac66235-69dc-4092-b430-9d68837e0c76", "content_type": "generic", "workflow_state": "public", "page_title": "Pipelines", "short_description": "What a pipeline is in Godzilla: a named, versioned workflow that moves data from a source connector through transform steps to a destination.", "body": "

Pipelines

A pipeline is the core unit of work in Godzilla: a named, versioned data-processing workflow that moves data from a source connector, through zero or more transform steps, to a destination connector. Every pipeline runs as a sequence of events flowing through that path.

Anatomy of a pipeline

Every pipeline has three parts:

  • Source — the connector that emits events into the pipeline (a database, a queue, an upload, a webhook).
  • Transforms — an ordered list of steps that reshape, filter, or enrich events as they pass through. Transforms are optional; a pipeline with none is a pass-through copy.
  • Destination — the connector that events are written to once transforms complete.
{{ds:component/alert|variant=info|title=Pipelines are declarative|body_html=

You describe the desired source, transforms, and destination; Godzilla schedules and retries the runs. You never manage worker processes directly.

}}

Pipeline state

A pipeline is always in one of three states:

  • draft — configured but not yet processing events.
  • active — running on its configured schedule or trigger.
  • paused — temporarily stopped; resumes from the last checkpoint.

Versioning

Pipeline configuration is versioned. Publishing a new version does not affect events already in flight on the previous version — in-flight runs finish on the version they started on. This matters most when a pipeline definition is part of a larger migration; see the Migration guide for an example of retiring an old pipeline version safely.

Next steps

Ready to build one? Start with the Building your first pipeline guide, or jump straight to the Pipelines endpoint in the API reference.

Glossary

Short definitions for every term used throughout these docs.

Pipeline
A named, versioned workflow that moves data from a source connector, through optional transforms, to a destination connector.
Connector
A pre-built integration to an external system — a source, a destination, or both.
Event
The atomic unit of data moving through a pipeline, or a platform lifecycle notification like pipeline.failed.
Webhook
An outbound HTTP request Godzilla sends to a URL you control when a subscribed event occurs.
Dead-letter queue
Where an event goes after exhausting its retries, rather than being dropped. See Handling errors & retries.

The pagination style used by every v2 list endpoint. See Rate limits & errors.
Workspace
The top-level account boundary an API key is scoped to.

args.short_description: Reshape, filter, and enrich events as they pass through a pipeline.
args.body:
Transforming events in flight

Transforms are intermediate processing steps applied to events as they travel between a source connector and a destination in a pipeline. You can use transforms to reshape payload structures, filter out unwanted records, and enrich events with additional context.

1. Reshaping events

Use reshape transforms to rename fields, restructure nested objects, or strip sensitive and unneeded keys before writing to downstream storage.

{{ds:component/code-block|filename=reshape-transform.json|language=json|code={ \"type\": \"reshape\", \"config\": { \"rename\": { \"customer_email\": \"email\", \"amt_cents\": \"amount_cents\" }, \"drop\": [\"internal_notes\", \"raw_ip\"] } }}}

2. Filtering events

Filtering lets you conditionally route or drop events based on payload criteria. Non-matching events are discarded immediately, saving destination throughput and storage.

{{ds:component/code-block|filename=filter-transform.json|language=json|code={ \"type\": \"filter\", \"config\": { \"condition\": \"payload.status == 'completed' && payload.amount_cents > 0\" } }}} {{ds:component/alert|variant=info|title=Dropped events|body_html=

Filtered-out events do not trigger retries or dead-letter queue entries; they are treated as successfully skipped.

}}

3. Enriching events

Enrichment transforms add metadata, computed values, or static contextual fields to the event payload before delivery.

{{ds:component/code-block|filename=enrich-transform.json|language=json|code={ \"type\": \"enrich\", \"config\": { \"add_fields\": { \"environment\": \"production\", \"processed_by\": \"godzilla-pipeline-v2\"\n } } }}}

Configuring transforms in a pipeline

Transforms are supplied as an ordered array on the pipeline definition. Godzilla executes each transform sequentially for every event.

{{ds:component/code-block|filename=pipeline-with-transforms.json|language=json|code={ \"name\": \"orders-with-transforms\", \"source_connector_id\": \"conn_pg_orders\", \"destination_connector_id\": \"conn_snowflake_dw\", \"transforms\": [\n { \"type\": \"filter\", \"config\": { \"condition\": \"payload.amount_cents > 0\" } }, { \"type\": \"reshape\", \"config\": { \"drop\": [\"raw_ip\"] } }, { \"type\": \"enrich\", \"config\": { \"add_fields\": { \"region\": \"us-east\" } } } ] }}} {{ds:component/alert|variant=warning|title=Order of execution matters|body_html=

Because transforms run sequentially, placing filter steps first avoids unnecessary processing on events that will ultimately be dropped.

}}

Next steps

Learn how Godzilla deals with transformation and destination write failures in Handling errors & retries, configure steps via the Transforms endpoint, or manage your pipelines directly using the Pipelines endpoint.

{{ds:component/docs-pagination|prev_href={{cms:item/93eecc21-ad7e-43ae-a9d5-a0301ad65f1d}}|prev_label=Connecting a data source|next_href={{cms:item/c484e924-5ec5-4c95-81ad-c8c31b702a7f}}|next_label=Handling errors & retries}}

{{ds:component/code-block|filename=enrich-transform.json|language=json|code={ \"type\": \"enrich\", \"config\": { \"add_fields\": { \"environment\": \"production\", \"processed_by\": \"godzilla-pipeline-v2\"\n } } }}}

{{ds:component/code-block|filename=pipeline-with-transforms.json|language=json|code={ \"name\": \"orders-with-transforms\", \"source_connector_id\": \"conn_pg_orders\", \"destination_connector_id\": \"conn_snowflake_dw\", \"transforms\": [\n { \"type\": \"filter\", \"config\": { \"condition\": \"payload.amount_cents > 0\" } }, { \"type\": \"reshape\", \"config\": { \"drop\": [\"raw_ip\"] } }, { \"type\": \"enrich\", \"config\": { \"add_fields\": { \"region\": \"us-east\" } } } ] }}} {{ds:component/alert|variant=warning|title=Order of execution matters|body_html=

Because transforms run sequentially, placing filter steps first avoids unnecessary processing on events that will ultimately be dropped.

}}

args.short_description: Reshape, filter, and enrich events as they pass through a pipeline.
args.body:
Transforming events in flight

Transforms are intermediate processing steps applied to events as they travel between a source connector and a destination in a pipeline. You can use transforms to reshape payload structures, filter out unwanted records, and enrich events with additional context.

1. Reshaping events

Use reshape transforms to rename fields, restructure nested objects, or strip sensitive and unneeded keys before writing to downstream storage.

{{ds:component/code-block|filename=reshape-transform.json|language=json|code={ "type": "reshape", "config": { "rename": { "customer_email": "email", "amt_cents": "amount_cents" }, "drop": ["internal_notes", "raw_ip"] } }}}

2. Filtering events

Filtering lets you conditionally route or drop events based on payload criteria. Non-matching events are discarded immediately, saving destination throughput and storage.

{{ds:component/code-block|filename=filter-transform.json|language=json|code={ "type": "filter", "config": { "condition": "payload.status == 'completed' && payload.amount_cents > 0" } }}} {{ds:component/alert|variant=info|title=Dropped events|body_html=

Filtered-out events do not trigger retries or dead-letter queue entries; they are treated as successfully skipped.

}}

3. Enriching events

Enrichment transforms add metadata, computed values, or static contextual fields to the event payload before delivery.

{{ds:component/code-block|filename=enrich-transform.json|language=json|code={ "type": "enrich", "config": { "add_fields": { "environment": "production", "processed_by": "godzilla-pipeline-v2" } } }}}

Configuring transforms in a pipeline

Transforms are supplied as an ordered array on the pipeline definition. Godzilla executes each transform sequentially for every event.

{{ds:component/code-block|filename=pipeline-with-transforms.json|language=json|code={ "name": "orders-with-transforms", "source_connector_id": "conn_pg_orders", "destination_connector_id": "conn_snowflake_dw", "transforms": [ { "type": "filter", "config": { "condition": "payload.amount_cents > 0" } }, { "type": "reshape", "config": { "drop": ["raw_ip"] } }, { "type": "enrich", "config": { "add_fields": { "region": "us-east" } } } ] }}} {{ds:component/alert|variant=warning|title=Order of execution matters|body_html=

Because transforms run sequentially, placing filter steps first avoids unnecessary processing on events that will ultimately be dropped.

}}

Next steps

Learn how Godzilla deals with transformation and destination write failures in Handling errors & retries, configure steps via the Transforms endpoint, or manage your pipelines directly using the Pipelines endpoint.
